answer: A sponsor carries 68% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the ivory liability is written down in the ferrous ledger at admission, the copper audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must thus place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 12 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
